isolation_strategies.label: Schema per tenant
isolation_strategies.description: Each {{ multi_tenancy_term }} lives in its own Postgres schema; a global schema holds shared catalogues (users, roles, vocabulary, parameters). Hibernate switches search_path per connection via a custom MultiTenantConnectionProvider.

positives: Strong isolation: backup, restore, retention and audit per {{ multi_tenancy_term }}.
Migrations applied N+1 times (1 global + N per {{ multi_tenancy_term }}) — explicit and auditable.
Cross-{{ multi_tenancy_term }} reports use explicit UNION ALL across schemas — protects against accidental leak.
Per-{{ multi_tenancy_term }} dump/restore is trivial — useful for GDPR/LGPD right-to-erasure or moving a {{ multi_tenancy_term }} to another instance.
negatives: Cross-{{ multi_tenancy_term }} queries require explicit code (no automatic JOIN).
New {{ multi_tenancy_term }} = new migration set (schema + every V*.sql) — automated but adds an operational step.
DDL drift risk: all emp_* schemas must be on the same migration version. The migrations service is the single source of truth.

isolation_strategies.label: Tenant-id column
isolation_strategies.description: Single schema; every row carries a tenant_id column. Filter applied universally via Hibernate @Filter or query interceptor at the EntityManager level.

positives: Single schema simplifies migrations and backup operations.
Cross-{{ multi_tenancy_term }} queries are trivial — just drop the filter where allowed.
negatives: Risk of leak if the filter is forgotten in custom native queries.
Heavier indexes — every secondary index must include tenant_id to remain selective.
Single backup/restore — harder to operate per-{{ multi_tenancy_term }} retention or GDPR-style erasure.

isolation_strategies.label: Database per tenant
isolation_strategies.description: Each {{ multi_tenancy_term }} in a separate Postgres database, with its own connection pool. The application maintains N HikariCP DataSources and resolves which one to use per request.

positives: Strongest isolation — physical separation, easy to move a {{ multi_tenancy_term }} to a different host.
Per-{{ multi_tenancy_term }} resource limits possible at the DB level.
negatives: N connection pools at runtime — memory + handshake cost scales linearly.
Complex local development (N databases to seed).
Schema migrations harder to orchestrate (must hit every DB).

isolation_strategies.label: Single-tenant
isolation_strategies.description: No tenant isolation — the application serves a single internal {{ multi_tenancy_term }}. No tenant_id is propagated; the request context is empty of tenant data.

positives: Simplest model — no holder, no filter, no propagation.
negatives: Cannot serve multiple tenants without a non-trivial refactor.

modes.label: Multi-empresa (group)
modes.description: Corporate multi-tenant: N known units of the same economic group share users, RBAC and master catalogues; only operational data differs per unit. Tenants are pre-registered and known at design time. For SaaS with unknown external clients (dynamic tenant discovery), use the `multi-tenant` mode instead.

modes.label: Multi-tenant (SaaS B2B)
modes.description: SaaS multi-tenant: external clients isolated as dynamically-discovered tenants. Tenants are unknown at design time. RBAC is per-tenant; catalogues may be shared or per-tenant depending on product design.

modes.label: Single-tenant
modes.description: Internal project without isolation. No tenant_id propagation. Use when the application has exactly one consumer organisation.

sync.enforcement_description: Every application.service method MUST call holder.require() at entry, enforced by an ArchUnit rule. Forgetting it raises a compile-time test failure rather than a silent runtime leak.

async.cleanup_description: ThreadLocal does not cross thread boundaries. The {{ multi_tenancy_term }} id travels as a JMS message header; the consumer reads it, binds the holder, processes, and calls holder.clear() in a finally block. Failing to clear leaks state across thread-pool reuse — this is mandatory.
